q1_issues.issue: A bare generic verbal rule with no quantifier word takes strength 0.9 ('Birds fly' -> STV 0.9 0.9); strength 1.0 is reserved for an explicit all/every, so (STV 1.0 0.9) overstates the generalization.

q2_gaps: The temporal-proximity adverb 'soon' has no licensed slot - it falls in the sequence/ordering-adverb family the instruction set directs you to leave out and record - so the parse silently loses it.

A bare MASS noun as subject of a verbal generic ('Salt-bloom dissolves ...'): the instruction set licenses the distributing rule only for a bare plural or an explicit quantifier, and gives no reading for quantifying (Member $x salt_bloom) over instances of a mass kind.
notes: Both compound genus atoms (salt_bloom->bloom, seawater->water) are right, the noun modifiers are correctly left unexposed, and the definite 'the seawater' is properly a top-level constant outside the rule; Goal for 'into the seawater' is the licensed motion-result oblique.
